origin.description: Herfindahl concentration coefficient of a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measure is defined for non-negative values.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result missing.

origin.details: Shares are the values divided by their sum. With parameter m the coefficient sums those shares raised to m+1 and raises that sum to 1/m. The default m is 1, which is the sum of squared shares. conc() calls this when type is Herfindahl, and a NULL parameter there also selects 1.
origin.value: A single number, the Herfindahl coefficient.
origin.example:
# generate vector (of sales)
x <- c(541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261)
# compute Herfindahl coefficient with parameter 1
Herfindahl(x)

translation.description: Herfindahl concentration coefficient of a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. The measure is defined for non-negative values. Missing values are NaN.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Exponent m. None uses 1, including when conc() passes its default through.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If true, drop missing values first. If false, any missing value makes the result NaN. This is na.rm in R.

translation.details: Shares are the values divided by their sum. With parameter m the coefficient sums those shares raised to m+1 and raises that sum to 1/m. The default m is 1, which is the sum of squared shares. The arithmetic is NumPy. conc() calls this when type is Herfindahl.
translation.value: A single number, the Herfindahl coefficient.
translation.example:
from ineq.concentration import Herfindahl

# generate vector (of sales)
x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
# compute Herfindahl coefficient with parameter 1
print(Herfindahl(x))
